utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-69-T, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll continue today with the housekeeping sessions and I will first deal with a few follow-ups from last Thursday. First, I think it was announced that the revised B/C/S version of P1050 would be available I think already on that Thursday. Is it there?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's uploaded as 65 ter 267.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the document was already admitted, the revised B/C/S version may now replace the old one. And, Madam Registrar, you are instructed accordingly. We briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. It seems, Mr. Jordash, that the issue of a disputed translation of the words, [B/C/S spoken], seems to have been resolved with CLSS. CLSS agreeing with the Stanisic Defence. May I then take it that the Stanisic Defence withdraws its request and then, of course, the Chamber would not require any further submission under Rule 33(B) from the Registry. Mr. Jordash, is it moot?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, if that seems to be the easiest way to deal with things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the request is withdrawn, the request for further verification of the translation and the Chamber for the same reason doesn't require any 33 (B) submissions from the Registry anymore. Madam Registrar, that is on the record hereby. Then I note that CLSS has provided a revised translation for P1628, and I already did put on the record last week that P1628 was vacated, so we should really speak about P2545, and the Registry is instructed to replace the old English translation of P2545 with the revised one. Just to make sure, has that translation, that revised translation been uploaded?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the instruction stands. Next on my agenda is to continue with the MFI list. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are some document which we think were missed out along the way and they start with D245.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look. D245.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There were five documents, D245, D248, D249, D250, D251, and D271 needed to be tendered by us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me have a look -- yes, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe we did deal with this last week and the -- we requested further information about provenance for all of those except D271, which is the chart, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We've sent provenance on each one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we check this during the first break, that you seek to agree on where we stand in this respect, and that I'll then hear from you, and that is D245, you said, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: D245, D248, D249, D250, and D251, and D271 to be tendered, and most of them were sent to the Prosecution on the 3rd of July, or re-sent on the 3rd of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And in relation to -- sorry, Your Honour. In relation to D271, I can inform Your Honour, this doesn't depend upon the Prosecution's agreement, I don't think. The document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the issue was whether the -- if we have dealt with all the underlying documents, that -- and if there are objections or if some of these documents have to be taken out, that then the chart should be amended accordingly, and that's, therefore, it's the last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: A corrigendum cover page has been uploaded as 1D04899.1. It's released in e-court and can be attached to 271 with the underlying issues having been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we've reviewed the corrigendum and we agree that that resolves that issue of the typo in the -- in the chart. So from our perspective that can be attached. We do maintain that we would like all the underlying documents to be resolved first before the chart is admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, therefore, Madam Registrar, you are instructed to upload the new cover page, the corrected corrigendum cover page and no decision has yet been taken on admission of the chart. Then I think we had dealt with the last one is D293 and, therefore, we are now at D301. I think here we are in a similar position. We first have to deal with the underlying documents before we can finally decide on the chart D301. Underlying documents are D302, and I go through them very quickly. Any objections against D302?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: One moment, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The series of underlying documents runs from D302 up to and including D311, and there were two where there was a translation issue, but let's first focus on objections.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have a bit of a submission on this document. At the time that it was tendered we objected because it was the statement of another individual who wasn't called to testify. Now, the Defence made arguments about that in court, that's with respect to D302. We note first that the Defence did initially object to the admission of the Kojic statement when it was tendered on the 10th of December. According to the list of pending issues compiled by the Prosecution during the Prosecution case, the Defence maintained its objection at a meeting between the parties on the 7th of February, 2011. The Defence only withdrew that objection after the Prosecution filed a detailed written submission about its admissibility and reliability on the 9th of February, 2011. In that submission, the Prosecution argued that the Chamber should proceed with caution when admitting a hearsay statement under Rule 89(C) [Realtime transcript read in error "90(C)"] due to the inability to cross-examine the witness, but we provided detailed reasons why this particular statement was authentic, relevant, and reliable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I first ask you to -- I see that "hearsay statement under Rule 90(C)" but I think I heard ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you said 98 but whatever it is 89(C).

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: My apologies. We argued, among other factors, that the Kojic statement was reliable due to the fact that it was firsthand and that its contents were not subject to failures of perception or memory. It was the individual's own statement about his own position in the MUP during 1991. The Prosecution would request the Defence to explain the authenticity, relevance, and reliability of this five-page statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are now talking about D302.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: D302, yes, Your Honour, in the same way as those submissions were made before. So we are awaiting those submissions from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Are you able to make those submissions immediately, or, Mr. Jordash, otherwise we'll leave it --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, I can't make them immediately. But I would say only this for the record, that if -- the Prosecution's chronology is correct, but we haven't accepted, just for the record, that the Kojic stent is reliable. So just for the record. But we'll make our submissions on this. In relation to relevance, we would say it's obvious, but we'll make submissions about reliability, this statement on the face of it, is -- cannot be distinguished from the Kojic statement and if that's admissible, so is this. But we'll make detailed submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll hear from you. Then we move on to D303. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: With respect to D303, all the way up to and including D311, we are awaiting information about provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To be provided by the Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That's not completely accurate. 303, I think the Prosecution are waiting for information. 304, that's correct; 305 ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was an incorrect English translation in relation to D305. Has that been --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, that's been uploaded under 1D02395.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the issue of provenance is still there apparently.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That document, we've told the Prosecution, was received from the accused. We've made a request from the National Council to see if we can obtain that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I think we had -- Ms. Marcus extended the issue from D303 up to and including D311, which would mean that the provenance is still apparently is not settled or not satisfactorily.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: They are all from the first accused and we've made the request to the National Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so we'll wait for an answer on all of those. There was one other translation issue which was D310 was the missing English translation, but I think that was only housekeeping session filing, so has that English translation been uploaded? I should look at you, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Can I just have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest that we continue anyhow because for other reasons the document is not yet ready for admission, so take your time to check whether the missing English translation has now been uploaded. And D302, being the chart, and D303 up to and including D311, they remain on the MFI list. We move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, apparently the translation is attached to 310.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is now attached so that -- Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just wanted to resolve some issues we just spoke about five minutes ago, unless you want me to hold it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can briefly do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Very briefly, yes. With respect to D245, D248, D249, D250 and D251. These are all from RFAs, so we drop our objection to admission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which means that D245, D248, D249, D250, and D251 are all admitted into evidence. And as far as I can see, there's no need for protection, or is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think it's best that we check those. They are DB reports so there may be material --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then all the numbers I just mentioned are provisionally under seal. Let me see whether in those series there's still -- I'll check that during the next break whether there is any other matter related to those documents outstanding. Then we move on to D319. There were two issues. First Prosecution was trying to look into the origins of the video and could not provide a response, can you now, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. According to the information we were able to find out, this video footage is from a documentary created by Pavle Vranjican and Mr. Vranjican created a compilation of various film footage which all seem to originated in the Yutel archive. The Prosecution is concerned that even though the underlying footage appears to be authentic, it has been clearly cut and edited. The parts showing Pupovac and the parts showing Babic and the others take up a different amount of the screen indicating that it's not one continuous video. It would be very difficult to accept that this video depicts Babic and other members of the Knin political elite laughing at Pupovac's speech and walking out of the hall as stated by the presenter. With respect -- that's with respect to the first clip. With respect to the second clip, again it appears to be authentic film footage, but we submit with respect to that clip that the Chamber should give it very little weight due to it being the comments of an unidentified person who sounds as though he is speculating about much of what he says. With respect to the third clip, it is again an unidentified soldier. The date of 29 September, 1991, does appear on the footage, but there is no basis for the introductory shot which says that this took place in Glina. The Prosecution submits that if the Chamber decides to accept that third portion for admission, it should give very little weight to the conclusions drawn by the presenter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, for clips 2 and 3, you said don't give much weight to it. The first one, is that to be understood as a objection against admission or just as a caveat?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: That's an objection against admission, Your Honour, for the first clip.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At this moment D319 is one exhibit, isn't it? Any further response? Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the assertions of my learned friends are unfounded. If we look at the first part, it is obvious that it's always the same room, the same time, and the same participants. One part may have been clipped out, but it is clearly the same event being filmed by a camera. The remarks of my learned friend may be -- portend as to the weight that should be given to that evidence. In our mind --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The second and third clip, apparently there's no objection against admission, and the Chamber will start from that point of view. Ms. Marcus -- I take it that you would argue that there's nothing against admission of the second and the third clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then what remains in dispute is the first clip. Mr. Petrovic has given his view, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I have no reply, Your Honour, other than to repeat what our position is, Your Honour, and we maintain that with respect to the first clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, I would like to add one sentence. One of the crucial pieces of evidence of the Prosecution, the film titled "Unit" consists of two hours of edited clips showing footage with different people from different periods and it seems to me that the objection is really inappropriate when it is obvious that all is about the same event filmed for one broadcast. Whereas in contrast, the other piece of evidence is a compilation of various things par excellence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I would like to, at some stage, join in this argument but I thought that what we were doing is discussing admissibility, so I would respectfully ask that the Prosecution restrain from making submissions as to weight until it's appropriate to do so, until we can all engage in the process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, until now I understood it mainly to be that there's no objection against admission and you would urge the Prosecution that if they do not really object, that they should refrain at this moment from commenting on the weight to be given.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's not spend too much time on that. What we'll do -- you wanted to respond, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Just one brief point, Your Honour, which is that with respect to the "Unit" video, we do not rely on the words of the presenter, we said that repeatedly. This is a very different situation where the words are the presenter are the portion we feel we contest and the conclusions are not -- that the presenter draws are not conclusions that we believe can necessarily be drawn from the footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the best we can do is have a look at it and see to what extent we are convinced both on the basis of the text and on the basis of what we see, whether we would admit or not. Now, there was also another matter, Mr. Petrovic, I think an English translation was there to be uploaded. Has that been done?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, both the English translation and the accompanying paper that goes with the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you mean the surrogate sheet? Or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So those issues then have been resolved. We'll first have a look at it, Ms. Marcus, and then once we've decided about the first clip, then we also know whether we have to make a separation between the -- between the three clips depending on whether we'll grant your objection, yes or no. D319, therefore, remains on the list of documents or in this case video marked for identification. I move on to D327. Ms. Marcus, I think that D327 is the chart of comments on exhibits. It will depend on the underlying documents, I take it, whether you object or not. Is that still your position?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: We actually dropped our objections to the remaining underlying document, that was D328 and D329. We, therefore, drop our objection to the admission of the chart as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, they are already admitted under seal as a matter of fact. So, therefore, D327 is admitted under seal. I move on to D330. Let me have a look. You were seeking additional information, Ms. Marcus, on the provenance. Have you received such information?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Not to my knowledge, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's the same position; from the client, we are seeking information from the National Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that remains on our list for the time being. Could we urge the National Council to or could you perhaps inform that the Chamber would very much like to have these matters resolved and once you would need our intervention, Mr. Jordash, don't hesitate to seek it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we move on to D331. There on the 19th of July, the -- it was said that the Prosecution still needed to discuss the document with the Stanisic Defence. On my list it's unclear what exactly you would like to discuss. If it's provenance, then we might get to a similar position, but I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We have no objection to this document being tendered from the bar table.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, D331 is admitted into evidence. We move to D332. That is an Official Note of the SR Krajina SUP Knin. The issue here is whether D332, marked for identification, is the same as D98 which is already admitted. First of all, Mr. Petrovic, has the Simatovic Defence received the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. The original has been uploaded as 2D535.2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And are you sure that it's not the same as D98?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise, I need to check that. I don't have it readily available. I don't have that information readily available. I have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then, please, verify that to start with. Would you then have a look at the translations, the translations are more or less the same, but not exactly, so if you have any preference for the one or the other translation, again it's only minor differences, and none of them apparently affecting the meaning of the document. Could you then choose, inform the other parties of your preferred translation, and then finally, if it's one document to have it most likely then the translation, the preferred translation attached to D98. If there are different documents, then, still, I think if the original text is the same, it would be preferable to have also the same translation. But if you could please verify this and then inform the Chamber. I can't say that the list is quickly getting much longer. Apart from that, Madam Registrar, at least D332, whether it stands or not, should be replaced by the original, to replace the copy which was uploaded until now. Let me just check, Mr. Petrovic, whether ... Yes, you have given the number to Madam Registrar, the number under which the original was uploaded, so may I take it, Madam Registrar, that replacing the copy which was initially uploaded by the originals causes no problems. Then I have a series of four documents. That is D357, D360, D361, and D362. The issue was whether the Prosecution maintains its objection, but I have to add to that that for D360 and D361 the final solution of what I briefly call the 54 bis issue may at this moment be an obstacle to -- yes, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's right, but that is not true for D357 and D362?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: 362 are from the client, again to be requested from the National Council. And in relation to 357, the issue is one of redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There was -- I have got on my list that the Prosecution wanted to check the original RFA, but if you received it from your client, Mr. Jordash, then I take it that there's no --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, it's both issues, actually, redactions and we need to receive it from the National Council if they have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that means that all four, two for the 54 bis reasons and the two others, that is D357 and D362 still waiting for further information about the provenance. I'm not very successful in shortening my MFI list, but I'm still -- I do not give up my hope. The next one is D363. Mr. Jordash, the objection was relevance. Could you please explain to the Chamber what the relevance is. I think it was a lot of press clippings or a report on what appeared in the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It's a Croatian media summary summarising certain reports from UN Commission for Human Rights, and a number of other issues such as speeches given by persons such as the parliamentary speaker, Tomcic [phoen], on Dayton Accords. Actually, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's summarising media, what appeared in the media, and the question is to what extent that is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I have five minutes. I do apologise, Your Honour. I just want to check this before talking off the top of my head.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five minutes are granted. You might even have to wait until after the break, Mr. Jordash. D364. There, the issue was that the witness was not able to provide much context for the document which was an instruction on admission of volunteers to the JNA. I, in court, noted that the temporal and geographical scope of the instruction was at least unclear, and the Stanisic Defence asked the document to be marked for identification while it clears up the question raised by me and perhaps the objection raised by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: My understanding was that the Prosecution had removed their objection to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my question remains temporal/geographical scope. I see here the Stanisic Defence asked that the document be MFI'd while it clears up the questions raised by Judge Orie. That's what I find on my list. There was, as far as I see, there was no objection against the document to be marked for identification. It's not entirely clear to me whether there also was no objection against admission.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: We drop our objection at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Mr. Jordash, any answer to my question temporal and geographical scope, or do you want another five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry, could I have another five minutes. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that makes ten. I move on to D365. Instruction on the acceptance of volunteers in the TO. Apparently taken from a book and listed as attachment number 7. Here again the Stanisic Defence asked that the document be MFI'd while it cleared up the document's origins, and the Prosecution did not object to marking it for identification. No objection against admission either.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this one, this document seems to be a retyped document, not the original or not an image of the original, so given that this is a law, it appears to us that the Defence should be able to obtain the original document rather than one that's been typed up, so that the cross-referencing, et cetera, the original law we wouldn't object to, to the admission, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: We will write to the National Council to try to obtain the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I hope that this is not becoming five months instead of five minutes to resolve, but -- and that also then if you receive it in that way, then also the question marks to what it was attached as attachment number 7 then may disappear as well. I move on to D366, again origin.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Prosecution have withdrawn their objection. We provided evidence of provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus, if that's the case ...

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of us withdrawing our objection, but I take Mr. Jordash at his word, it might have happened in an e-mail communication that I'm not ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: From Mr. Farr on the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Fair enough. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D366 is admitted into evidence. I move on to D367. It was MFI'd but the first thing was that the translation had to be uploaded. It has been uploaded. Now, any objections still standing, Ms. Marcus, in relation to the origin?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, 18th of August, 2011, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I take it that you'll partially accept Mr. Jordash's submissions, Ms. Marcus, and, therefore, D367 is admitted into evidence. D368. It was MFI'd because there was no B/C/S translation. It has been uploaded now and as far as I am aware of, there were no objections. The same is true for D369. No comments? Then D368 and D369 are admitted into evidence. D372, again, is a chart. The underlying documents are found in D374 up to and including D394 although there's one exception, that is that D382 was - that's a Hadzic special Ilok unit information report - was not one of the underlying documents. It was a document tendered by the Simatovic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Your Honour, this is a 1D document that we used and my learned friends from the Stanisic team informed us that they requested from the Croatian state to identify documents including this one, and that the application has already been submitted or is about to be submitted. I'm not sure. In any case, this is the information that I received from my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I made a mistake when I said that the underlying documents went up to D394 because the list is by far shorter. The first underlying documents being D374, D375, and D376, objections were about provenance. Do they still stand?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: D374, we have no further objections to that document. For D375 we are still awaiting provenance information and also there are redactions in that document. And D376 we are awaiting information as to provenance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, did I phrase the procedural matter you raised well enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we'll leave that open. Any other comment, Ms. Marcus?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. With respect to D420.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D420, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: We were asked whether it should be under seal, and we do suggest that it be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D420 is from now on under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: But may I add to that, Your Honour, that it -- the matter was -- this matter of this document was not addressed in the Chamber's invitation to Serbia, so although it does appear on the face of the document that it would likely contain at least some names of active members and should, therefore, be under seal, so we would put it in the Chamber's hands as to who should ask, whether it's for the Chamber, perhaps to invite Serbia on this document or for the Defence since it's their document but this any case at the moment I don't think Serbia is seized of this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although the Chamber considers the public character of the trial very important, this seems to come down to such a detail that we for very practical reasons refrain from taking any further steps and have the document and it was D420, under seal. Ms. Marcus, I'm looking at the clock, how much more time would you need?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I have nothing further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing further. Any other matter, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I kindly ask you to grant me five minutes to give you some information about a document as you instructed me a short while ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which document is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D98 and D332, Your Honour. The situation with these documents is rather unclear, and basically these are -- these two documents are the same. D98 contains the original document and a good translation of the document, whereas D332 includes the same document as a photocopy from the collection of Croatian documents and with D332 there is a translation of the photocopy from the book. We submitted the original document received from the Republic of Croatia, which is 2D535.2, which is an original document. However, it differs from the original and could in D98 in the stamp in the upper right-hand corner, which was placed there by the relevant authorities of the Republic of Croatia who stamped it when they were -- before they sent us this document. So that this last document, 2D535.2 is actually the most genuine, but it doesn't have a translation because this stamp placed by the Croatian authority is as yet untranslated. I believe that this may be confusing, but I'm awaiting your instructions, Your Honours. I hope I was able to explain it clearly enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is clear enough to me. Second question was whether you preferred one or the other translation? I suggest that the parties agree that the stamp put there by the Republic of Croatia is exclusively a stamp related to the delivery of the document or the -- indicating its source and that all parties can live without a translation of that stamp. Agreement?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's agreed. Now, the only thing you still have to do, Mr. Petrovic, is to find out which of the two translations you find the better one and we'll then focus on D -- let me just see. And could you repeat which one --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D98, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the one with the stamp but the original version.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's a document without a stamp. The original document with a valid translation. I believe that it would be best for all of us to use exclusively D98 in the future and that would be best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D332 is vacated as being as far as the content is concerned a duplicate of D98, and if you would prefer to have the translation of D98 to be replaced by the other translation, Mr. Petrovic, we'll hear from you. Any other matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that's necessary, Your Honours. And we don't have any further matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's not replaced. Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: A number of matters, if I may, which are related to the time that Your Honour gave me in large part. In relation to P3029 and the Prosecution's proposition that 65 ter 6271 should be added, we object. The Defence put part of a file to the witness Novakovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, sorry to interrupt you, I'm looking at the clock. I would then rather at this moment that you include that in short submissions on the leftovers to say so and then that we do not let the witness wait any longer and that we have -- there's only, if we take a break now we have only 50 minutes for the witness and I think it would be fair also for the witness to be heard. Unless there's any matter which you say it can be resolved by five words immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D363. That was relevance of the UNLO in Zagreb, that means D363 is no longer tendered and, therefore, is withdrawn and has status marked not admitted because you withdrew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH

utterances.text: Clear. We'll take a break. We will resume at ten minutes -- if possible, 20 minute break, would that do? I'm also looking at the Registry. We had a bit of a longer break earlier. Twenty minutes then. Then we'll resume at a quarter to 6.00 and then I expect the accused to be back and the witness to be standby to be examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I reserved five minutes for you at the end of this hearing, and I'd like you to strictly stay within that time-frame. Are you ready to call your next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be brought into the courtroom. Just to be sure, Mr. Jordash, no protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the 92 ter statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Grekulovic. Before you give evidence -- I'll start again. Can you hear me in a language you understand? Can you hear me in a language you understand, Mr. Grekulovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you by the usher. Could you please make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Grekulovic. Please be seated. First of all, our apologies that you had to wait for awhile. We'll continue to hear your evidence today for approximately a little bit over one hour and then tomorrow, and then if that's not enough time then the day after tomorrow. Mr. Grekulovic, you'll first be examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic. Please proceed, Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Grekulovic.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: You have a file at the side of you which I know contains exhibits. Perhaps it would be safer if the file was removed for now and if we want you to look at an exhibit, it can be brought up on the screen. Thank you. Could we have, first of all, your full name and date of birth for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC
utterances.text: Srdjan Grekulovic. I was born on the 20th of November, 1962.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could we have on the screen, please, 1D05266.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: What you are going to see, Mr. Grekulovic, is a document which purports to be your statement. Would you have a look at it and confirm whether this is your statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if we look at the bottom right-hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could enlarge the B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Do you recognise -- it's very faint, do you recognise your initials?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these are my initials.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And were you interviewed, as it says on the front of the document, on the 15th of September, 2011, and the 4th of October, 2011?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash, I take it it was a mistake that you wanted to ask whether it was his signature, his name, because the initials are of the other persons present.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that's understood. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review this document before you came to court and make any clarifications or amendments you wished to make?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC
utterances.text: I had an opportunity to read it. I did so, and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And during the process of it being compiled, did you have an opportunity to read it and clarify and make any amendments that you wished to make?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And what you have said in this statement is in accordance with the truth?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions in substance, you would give the same answers?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN GREKULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: May I tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...?

utterances.text: And may I tender the associated documents with this statement, those that have not been exhibited before.

utterances.text: 1D05139, 1D05138, 1D01607, 1D05134, 1D05133, 1D05136, 1D05137, 1D05131, 1D05132, 1D05130, 1D05135. utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Prosecution has no objection to the addition of these documents to the Stanisic Defence 65 ter list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are all -- leave is granted to add them to the 65 ter list. As far as admission is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no objection to any of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then all these documents are admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar, would you please tell me the numbers in the same sequence that is -- I'll just read the last four digits. 5139 which is in full 1D05139.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.text: 5137, am I mistaking, it's running from my screen that's the reason why ... let me see. We have had 5133, 5136, the next one is 5137.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will receive D529. 5131, D530.

utterances.text: All admitted under the numbers mentioned. Please proceed.

utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have on the screen, please, 1D05275.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Which is a map, Mr. Grekulovic, and would you have a look at it and confirm whether the locations marked are those that are most relevant to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH

utterances.text: We've received it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is Doboj, Teslic, Mrkonjic Grad, Banja Luka, Prijedor, Novi Grad and Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
